text: The Patriots' second encounter with Caleb Williams and the Bears didn't go any better than the first, as Chicago's young star orchestrated a 30-24 victory on Thursday Night Football in Week 7, with Williams throwing two touchdown passes to secure the win in Chicago. New England's offensive line took a significant hit heading into the contest—starting guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown were both ruled out, a pair of absences that likely contributed to Drake Maye's struggles against a Bears defense operating at full strength. On the bright side, running back Rhamondre Stevenson delivered an encouraging performance, reaching a career high in receiving yards while continuing to do the little things that keep the Patriots' offense afloat; the versatile back is now on the cusp of 100 carries for the sixth consecutive season, a testament to his consistency if not his team's overall fortunes. Mike Vrabel and his staff will have plenty to dissect from this one—both in terms of the offensive line injuries and the fundamental execution issues that allowed Williams and company to outscore them down the stretch.
